family.tagline: A loft desk, a busy kitchen and a nursery, run from one Companion Core.
family.story: Elena manages projects from a writing desk in the loft. Nikolai is home with one-year-old Mila, and the days run through the kitchen. One Companion Core sits on a shelf there.

companion.name: Nettle
companion.job: Drafts Elena’s weekly status note from the points she types.
companion.limits: Drafts only. Elena reads and sends every note herself.

companion.name: Barley
companion.job: Drafts Nikolai’s shopping list from the week’s meal plan.
companion.limits: Drafts the list only. Nikolai reads it and does the shopping.

popup.title: Mila crawls after the parcel
popup.body: Up the outside stair, a parcel waits. Nikolai carries it to the kitchen while Elena clears the shelf, and Mila crawls behind.

popup.title: Elena unwraps the Companion Core
popup.body: Elena finds the Companion Core inside, with a power cable, a quick-start guide and a recovery USB drive. Nikolai sets it on the kitchen shelf.

popup.title: Mila taps the power button
popup.body: On the shelf, Elena lifts Mila to tap the button. The Companion Core wakes and opens its own Wi-Fi network.

popup.title: Elena joins from her phone
popup.body: On her phone, Elena joins the Core’s own network from the Wi-Fi settings. Then she chooses the home network.

popup.title: The family picks the first apps
popup.body: In the Companion Hub store, Elena picks Hermes, and the family names its agents Nettle and Barley. Nikolai adds KitchenOwl and Nextcloud.

beats.capability: an agent that connects to chat apps, email and more from one self-hosted app

popup.title: Nettle says hello
popup.body: At the kitchen counter, Elena messages the agent she named Nettle. The reply comes from the Core.
popup.note: Messages pass through the chat service you choose.

say.speaker: elena
say.text: Hello, Elena. I am Nettle. Where shall we begin?

beats.capability: back up, search and organise your family photos and videos on your own Core

popup.title: Nikolai backs up the playground week
popup.body: Back home, Nikolai’s phone backs a week of playground photos up to Immich on the Core, not a photo cloud.
popup.note: Immich’s first start takes a while.

beats.capability: a shared grocery list, recipe book, meal planner and expense tracker for the household

popup.title: Lemons arrive from the loft
popup.body: From the loft, Elena adds lemons to the family list. At the island, Nikolai sees the new line, because KitchenOwl keeps one shared list on the Core.

beats.capability: an agent that connects to chat apps, email and more from one self-hosted app

popup.title: Nikolai checks the list Barley drafted
popup.body: While Mila’s porridge cools, Nikolai types the week’s meals to Barley. Barley drafts the list on the Core’s local model, and Nikolai reads it, then adds it to KitchenOwl.
popup.note: Messages pass through the chat service you choose.

say.speaker: nikolai
say.text: Here is the list from this week’s meals. Please check it.

beats.capability: a shared grocery list, recipe book, meal planner and expense tracker for the household

popup.title: The dumpling card can retire
popup.body: A dumpling recipe from his mother has lived on a stained card for years. Nikolai types it into KitchenOwl, and Elena can now cook from it too.

beats.capability: plan tasks and time blocks in one local file on your Core

popup.title: The plan follows a moved review
popup.body: The review moves a day earlier. From the loft sofa, Elena shifts the launch tasks, and Companion Planning keeps the plan as one local file.

beats.capability: scan and file your paperwork; it reads every page, tags it and makes it searchable

popup.title: Nikolai asks for a gas bill
popup.body: The permit form wants a utility bill, so Nikolai calls upstairs. Elena types one word, and Paperless-ngx finds last winter’s gas bill, read and tagged on the Core.

beats.capability: an agent that connects to chat apps, email and more from one self-hosted app

popup.title: Five points become the weekly note
popup.body: Friday morning, Elena types five points. With Companion Memory (beta) connected, Nettle drafts the weekly note, and Elena reads it and sends it herself.
popup.note: Messages pass through the chat service you choose.

beats.capability: your files, calendar and contacts on your own Core, synced to your devices

popup.title: Elena stops emailing herself
popup.body: After the engineer’s visit, Elena saves the new boiler warranty in Nextcloud. She stops emailing copies to herself, because the folder is on the Core.

beats.capability: your files, calendar and contacts on your own Core, synced to your devices

popup.title: Story hour reaches Elena’s phone
popup.body: Beside Mila on the sofa, Nikolai puts Saturday’s story hour into the family calendar. Nextcloud serves it from the Core, so Elena’s phone shows it too.

beats.capability: store every password in a vault you host, working with the Bitwarden apps

popup.title: Elena swaps a weak password
popup.body: At the living-room writing desk, Elena swaps the childcare portal’s weak password for a new one. VaultWarden keeps it in a vault the family hosts.

beats.capability: track every subscription you pay for and get a reminder before it renews

popup.title: Elena catches a trial before renewal
popup.body: A streaming trial is about to renew, and Wallos on the Core has already reminded Elena. By the fireplace, she and Nikolai decide to cancel it.

beats.capability: stream your own movies, shows and music to every screen in the house

popup.title: Elena chooses the afternoon film
popup.body: On her afternoon off, Elena picks the film in the family room downstairs. Jellyfin plays it from the family’s own collection on the Core to the TV.

beats.capability: stream your own movies, shows and music to every screen in the house

popup.title: Mila drums along to old songs
popup.body: Mila drums on the toy box while Nikolai plays the folder of songs Elena’s grandmother sang, copied from old tapes. Jellyfin plays them from the Core.

beats.capability: control and automate your smart home from one place, locally, without a cloud account

popup.title: Nikolai dims the nursery for naptime
popup.body: As Mila settles, Nikolai taps once and the nursery lamp turns low and warm. Home Assistant runs it from the Core, needing no cloud account of its own.

beats.capability: track your plants, watering and care history across rooms and beds, with a garden journal

popup.title: Nikolai waters, then writes it down
popup.body: Tuesday morning, Nikolai waters the bed under the willow. He logs it in HortusFox with a picture of the new leaves, and the journal keeps the date.

beats.capability: take notes and keep to-dos that sync across your devices through your own server

popup.title: Elena takes the call outside
popup.body: Elena takes the committee call on the side deck and types notes as she listens. Joplin Server syncs them to her laptop before she is back at her desk.

popup.title: From loft desk to kitchen shelf
popup.body: Status notes, meal plans, photos and the nursery lamp run from one Companion Core on the kitchen shelf.

closing.body: Your lists, photos and paperwork can sit on a Companion Core at home. Pick your first apps in the Companion Hub store.

notes: Elena’s loft beats anchor on the one writing desk, the sofa, the daybed and the room (couch nth 0 and 1 narrowed to office). living-vault uses the real writing desk in the main-floor living room. No bookshelf or laptop item is named.
Mila is a baby with no archetype or companion. nursery-songs carries her: she drums on the toy box while Nikolai plays the old tape songs.
First Companion Memory mention is loft-nettle (a film beat) and reads Companion Memory (beta). ftue-pick names no Memory.
No small-business beats: the household has no business. Wallos, Nextcloud, Paperless-ngx, VaultWarden and Joplin Server chips use the catalog replaces names only.

Hermes beats name who sends: Elena reads the weekly note and sends it herself; Barley drafts a shopping list and Nikolai does the shopping. No agent contacts a third party. Filed papers are the family’s own; no employer files.
Home Assistant runs the nap scene from the Core and needs no cloud account of its own; the beat says nothing about the lamp’s own app. No Zigbee claim.

The tv-stand is on the garden-level family room, so living-film says the family room downstairs. The fireplace and writing desk are in the main-floor living room; the crib and toy box are in the nursery.
